name: Gary Numan (style) — D minor 132
description: Modelled on the late-70s Gary Numan sound (The Pleasure Principle era) — original parts, not any of his songs. Tone stand-ins on the MacBook's GM synth (DLSMusicDevice): Minimoog bass → Synth Bass 1 p38 (p39 for a squelchier one); Polymoog "Vox Humana" ensemble → SynthStrings 1 p50, its brassy edge → SynthBrass 1 p62 an octave up; string machine → SynthStrings 2 p51; Minimoog lead → Saw Lead p81 (Square Lead p80 is the rounder option); a dry, tight real kit p0 with closed/open hats and syndrum-style tom fills. D minor at 132 bpm: pedal bass with octave jumps under Dm Bb C (A in the chorus). Rows 1-5 drums (ch 10), 6-9 bass SUBROUTINES and A-C bass (ch 13), D-E riff SUBROUTINES, F riff on strings (ch 15), G riff on brass and H pad (ch 16), I-K lead (ch 11), L-P sections, Q jam, R tone lab. Every row carries its level as "velocity". Row 0 plays the song.
prompt: Make a Gary Numan key bank. Approximate the tones in the original song with the synths and drums on the MacBook Pro. Show me train of thought
